lawyer:
Mr. M I Farooqui, Advocate, instructed by Mr. M.G. Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record ------ for the petitioner. 
Mr. Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record ------ for the Respondent No. 4 
Respondent Nos. 1-3: Not represented.
parties:
Asma Begum ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 7. Mr. M I Farooqui, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the petitioner by making representations to the prescribed authority discharged her onus that her whereabouts were known to the authority which did not receive due consideration by the High Court Division, that the High Court Division was wrong in not holding that the property was not an abandoned property in the absence of any opinion adverse to the petitioners activity and that the High Court Division misconstrued the ratio laid down in the cases of Bangladesh Vs. Md. Jalil and others, 48 DLR(AD)10; Rex Vs. Northumberland Compensation Appeal Tribunal (1952) 1KB338, and that in view of the materials on record, the High Court Division was wrong in not holding that the fundamental rights of the petitioner under Article 31, 42 and 48 of the Constitution have been violated by treating the property as an abandoned one.
